subject: Anthropology
title: Religion and Social Cohesion
description: One-minute skill: Religion and Social Cohesion.

hook.text: When a village prays together, shares a meal, and sings the same hymn, something binds them beyond words.

buildup.text: Durkheim argued that religion's primary function is to unite individuals into a moral community through shared rituals.

discovery.text: Collective rituals create solidarity. The shared emotional experience reinforces group identity and mutual obligation.

twist.text: Religion doesn't just unite — it also divides. It marks insiders from outsiders, believers from heretics.

climax.text: Religion is social glue and social wall. It binds communities together while drawing boundaries against others.

quiz.question: What did Durkheim say about religion's social function?
options: It unites individuals into a moral community through shared rituals

details.summary: Durkheim argued that religion's primary function is creating social solidarity by binding individuals into a moral community. Shared beliefs, rituals, and symbols generate collective effervescence — an emotional energy that reinforces group identity and commitment.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding religion as social glue explains its persistence even as supernatural beliefs decline. The social functions of religious community — belonging, meaning, mutual aid — fulfill needs no secular institution has fully replaced.
takeaways: Durkheim saw religion's primary function as social solidarity
Collective rituals generate emotional energy binding groups together
Religion fulfills social needs that secular institutions struggle to replace

faq.question: What is collective effervescence?
faq.answer: Collective effervescence is the heightened emotional energy that emerges when people gather for shared rituals. Think of the intense feeling at a religious revival, a football stadium, or a protest march. Durkheim argued this energy is what people experience as the sacred.

faq.question: Can religion also cause social division?
faq.answer: Absolutely. While religion bonds insiders together, it can also create sharp boundaries against outsiders. Religious identity has fueled wars, persecution, and discrimination. The same mechanisms that create in-group solidarity can generate inter-group conflict.
